title: Home Mining Weekly #2
subject: Home Mining Weekly #2: miner gift ideas and your first hour with a Bitaxe
preheader: Gift ideas by budget, this week's best prices, 3 new miners, and a first-hour Bitaxe setup checklist.
intro: The holidays are coming, and a small home miner makes a fun gift for anyone curious about Bitcoin. This week: gift ideas by budget, the best prices we found, 3 new miners, and what to do in your first hour with a Bitaxe.

feature.title: Gift ideas by budget
paras: We grouped the miners that are in stock right now by price: under $100, $100 to $300, and $300 and up. Each one has a line on who it suits, so you can pick for someone who just likes gadgets or someone who wants to heat a room.

Pre-order miners get their own section with a ship-date warning, so a gift doesn't arrive after the holidays. Black Friday is November 27, and our Black Friday page shows each miner's price today next to the lowest we've logged.

new_miners.blurb: Four chips for about 8.1 TH/s at 138 W, a big step up from a single-chip Bitaxe.
new_miners.name: NerdQX (8.1 TH/s)

new_miners.blurb: A new pre-order: about 3 TH/s at 33 W, €299 at Bitaxe.de, shipping from November 7.
new_miners.name: Nerdaxe Gaia Copper Pro

new_miners.blurb: Six chips on one Bitaxe board, about 4.2 TH/s at 90 W. Sold out right now, so set an alert.
new_miners.name: Bitaxe 702 (Supra Hex)

explainer.title: Your first hour with a Bitaxe
paras: Plug it in and the screen shows a setup Wi-Fi name and a QR code. Join it from your phone and put the miner on your home Wi-Fi. It only works with 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi.
Then open the miner's dashboard and change the pool's User field to your own Bitcoin address. Do the backup pool too. This is the step people skip, and it's where a block reward would go.
After about 10 minutes, check that accepted shares are going up and the hashrate looks normal for your board.
